audit.whatIsWrong: The entry attributes Quinn's blind to Vault (E) in six separate places — spikes[0], wants.you[0], wants.foe[0], whys[1], and the full layer's focus string and report[5] all say "Vault (Dash/Blind)" or "her E vault ... AND a blind". Vault does not blind. The blind is Blinding Assault (Q). The same strings also say Vault "knocks you back", which it does not.
audit.why: Riot's Vault text: "Quinn dashes to an enemy, dealing physical damage and slowing the target's Move Speed. Upon reaching the target, she leaps off the target, briefly interrupting it, and lands near her maximum Attack Range away from the target." It displaces HER, not you; what it does to you is a slow and a brief interrupt. Riot's Blinding Assault text is the one that hinders vision, and it is a separate ability on a separate 11/10.5/10/9.5/9 cooldown at 1025 range. This matters mechanically: the reader is told to bait one ability when the ability that actually beats them is a different one with a longer range and a different cooldown, so every "wait for it to be down" instruction in the entry points at the wrong clock.
audit.corrected: Blind reassigned to Blinding Assault throughout, with its 11s rank-1 cooldown; Vault restated as an interrupt plus self-peel that lands her at her own maximum attack range.
sources: champ-data/_kits/quinn.json (Q Blinding Assault cd 11/10.5/10/9.5/9 range 1025; E Vault cd 12/11/10/9/8 range 675)

audit.whatIsWrong: Behind Enemy Lines is named once, in passing, and its channel property is never stated — nor is the fact that Public Execution ends it.
audit.why: Riot's text: "Quinn and Valor team up to fly around at great speed" and the kit file flags it channel — interruptible by CC. Public Execution suppresses on arrival, and suppression is hard CC, so Ambessa's R cancels Quinn's R outright. That is the only tool Ambessa has against the roam that decides the late game in this matchup, and _missing-interactions.json flags it for exactly this pair.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level chart contradicts the prose it sits next to. Both layers open level 1 as "Skill" with the reason "Empowered-hit weaving wins the early AA exchanges", while the content layer's own early paragraph and whys[0] say "Levels 1-3 belong to Quinn" and "Quinn owns level 1". Level 3 is given to Quinn while whys[2] calls it "roughly even". phases[3].why is generic filler about banking small leads.
audit.why: Quinn is a ranged marksman with a periodic bonus-damage proc (Harrier) against a melee champion with one 650-range ability and a 70-energy cost per cast. There is no reading of level 1 in which Ambessa wins the auto-attack exchange. The correct shape is the packet's: Quinn, Quinn, Skill, Quinn, Ambessa, Ambessa, Quinn.
audit.corrected: Level 1 and levels 4-5 flipped to Quinn, level 3 flipped to Skill, in both layers; phases[0].why and phases[3].why rewritten to say why. Level 6 and first item should read "Ambessa" and could not be changed within the length band — left for the user.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[1].why claims "Dash-resets stack your passive shield mid-trade". Drakehound's Step produces no shield.
audit.why: Riot's Drakehound's Step text grants the next attack bonus range, damage and attack speed plus an energy refund. Ambessa's only shield is Repudiation (W). Against Quinn the distinction is the whole matchup: the spike is an empowered auto, and an empowered auto is exactly what a blind deletes.
audit.corrected: Rewritten to name what the passive actually gives and what Blinding Assault does to it.

audit.whatIsWrong: The packet flags this matchup as having no cooldown-sequencing advice anywhere, and that is accurate — not one number appears in either layer despite "track Vault before every commit" being the stated win condition.
audit.why: Blinding Assault is 11/10.5/10/9.5/9, Vault 12/11/10/9/8, Heightened Senses 50/45/40/35/30. The punishable one is Blinding Assault, because Ambessa's damage pattern routes through a basic attack; Vault only buys Quinn distance she already had.
audit.corrected: Numbers written into spikes[0], wants.you[0], whys[3], phases[3].why, breakdown.cooldowns and dontsFull[0].

audit.whatIsWrong: All three dontsFull descriptions are boilerplate that does not match their own titles: "Fight into her blind" is explained as "That is Quinn's favourite window", "Poke-war from range" as "Burning it for tiny value", and "Let her kite you out" as "Dumping every dash going IN". The same three strings are concatenated into report[11] as the Common Mistakes list.
audit.why: A mistake list where the explanation does not describe the mistake teaches nothing. Each one has a concrete answer available from the kits: the blind is on an 11s cooldown, her Q outranges Ambessa's Q 1025 to 650, and Vault deposits her a full attack range away.
audit.corrected: All three descriptions rewritten to explain their own titles with kit numbers.

The blind/Vault swap is the headline finding and the packet's suspectNames could not catch it: every ability NAME in this entry is spelled correctly, but the EFFECTS are attached to the wrong abilities. A name-distance scanner will never find this class of error. It is worth a separate sweep that cross-checks claimed effects against the kit descriptions rather than just names.

COULD NOT FIT IN THE BAND, for the user to apply by hand: content win[4] and win[5], and full phases[4].side and phases[5].side, should all read "Ambessa" — both layers' prose says level 6 is the swing and the Eclipse window is Ambessa's strongest, and the packet levelChart agrees.
